8517.t: CE6602: Construction Methods, Equipment, and Safety Management
8517.b:
Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : CE6602 : Construction Methods, Equipment, and Safety Management { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Construction Methods (8 hours)
Concrete construction, Batching and Mixing, Transportation and Placement, Finishing, Formwork, Scaffolding, Steel construction, Fabrication and erection, High-rise Buildings, Highways, Bridges, Underground Utilities, Tunnels, Offshore platforms.

Module 2 :

Prefabricated and Modular Construction (7 hours)
Prefabrication, Types of Prefabricated Structures, Planning for pre-casting, Design Considerations, Design Requirements for Safety Against Progressive Collapse, Joints, Stages of Precasting of Concrete Products, Tests For Components/Structures, Stacking, Handling Arrangements, Identification and Marking, Transport, Erection, Equipment, Modular Construction, Modular Co-ordination, Advantages and Limitations of Modular Construction.

Module 3 :

Construction Equipment (7 hours)
Construction Equipment Classification, Construction Equipment for Hoisting - Hoists, Crane, Factors Affecting Selection of Construction Equipment, Equipment Employment Cost, Depreciation Analysis - Straight line method, Sum of Years Digit method, Declining Balance method, Replacement of Equipment - Physical life, Profit life, Economic life, Intuitive method, Minimum cost method, Maximum profit method, Time Value method.
Module 4 :

Equipment for Earthwork (7 hours)
Earth-moving operations, Construction Earthwork Equipment: Tractor, Grader, Excavator, Roller. Bulldozer-Required power (Rolling resistance, Grade resistance), Available power, Usable power (Rimpull and Drawbar Pull), Performance Chart, Payload measurement methods- Gravimetric and Volumetric method, Bulldozer types, Blade adjustments, Productive dozing methods, Production estimation, Scraper - Scraper operations, Types, Production cycle, Scraper loading methods- Back-track loading, Chain loading, and Shuttle loading, Production estimation, Truck- Classification, Production cycle of truck, Production estimation.
Module 5 :

Other Construction Equipment (7 hours)
Equipment of Dredging- Dragline, Equipment of Trenching - Clam Shell, Equipment for De-watering - Pumping methods, and Electro-osmosis method, Equipment of grouting- Injection method, Slurry grouting, Chemical grouting, Compaction grouting, Jet grouting, Equipment for Demolition - Excavator, Bulldozer, Crusher, Hydraulic shear, Wrecking Balls, Cutting and Grinding Tools, Forklift, Dump Truck, Tunnelling - Percussion drilling, Rotary drilling, and Rotary Percussion drilling, Tunnel Boring Machine, Crane - Parts of crane, Principle of fulcrum, Crane motions- Travelling, Hoisting, Luffing, Slewing, Types of cranes- Lattice boom crawler crane, Lattice boom truck mounted cranes, Truck mounted telescopic crane, Modified cranes for heavy lifting, Tower crane- Top slewing tower crane, Bottom slewing tower crane, Mobile tower crane, Horizoontal boom tower crane, Luffing Jib tower crane, Articulated jib tower crane, Erection and Dismantling of tower crane, Factors affecting lifting capacity of crane, Guidelines for safe crane operations.

Course Objective

1 .

To study the basic construction methods associated with a construction project.
2 .

To study and understand the various types of equipment used for earthwork.
3 .

To study and understand the various types of equipment used for tunneling, drilling, blasting, dewatering, material handling conveyors, and their applications in construction projects.
4 .

To study and understand the importance of safety management related to a construction project.

Course Outcome

1 .

Develop knowledge of various construction methods in the construction industry.
2 .

Develop knowledge of prefabricated and module construction techniques.
3 .

Develop knowledge on planning and selection of equipment.
4 .

Explain the fundamentals of earthwork operations, earth-moving operations, and types of earthwork equipment.
5 .

Develop knowledge of special types of construction equipment and will be able to select the proper materials handling equipment.

Essential Reading

F. Harris, Modern Construction and Ground Engineering Equipment and Methods, Prentice Hall

2 .

Robert Peurifoy, Clifford J. Schexnayder,and Aviad Shapira, Construction Planning, Equipment and Methods, McGraw Hill

3 .

Granberg G., Popescu M, Construction Equipment and Management for Engineers, Estimators and Owners, Taylor and Francis Publishers, New York, 2006.

4 .

Edward Allen and Joseph Iano, Fundamentals of Building Construction: Materials and Methods, Wiley, Seventh Edition, 2019

Supplementary Reading

1 .

Deodhar, S.V. , Construction Equipment, and Job Planning, Khanna Publishers, New Delhi, 1988

2 .

Dr. Mahesh Varma, Construction Equipment, and its Planning and Application, Metropolitan Book Company, New Delhi. 1983.

3 .

Sharma, S. C. , Construction Equipment and Management, Khanna Publishing, First Edition, 2019.

4 .

Vijayan, D. S. Arvindan S. and Paulmakesh A., Construction Materials and Techniques, Notion Press, First Edition, 2021.

6213.b:
Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : EC6609 : Soft Computing { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Module-1: [8 Hours]
Fundamental Concepts: Introduction to Artificial Neural Networks (ANN), Models of a Neuron. Network structure Learning Process: Error–correction learning, Hebbian learning, competitive learning, Boltzmann learning, the credit-assignment problem, supervised learning, and other learning techniques.
Module-2: [11 Hours]
Single neuron/ Perceptron networks: Training methodology, typical application to linearly separable problems. Multilayer Perceptron: Back propagation algorithm, virtues and limitation of BP algorithm, modifications to back-propagation.
Module-3: [8 Hours]
Radial-basis function Networks – interpolation problem, Cover’s theorem, Regularization networks, Self-Organizing Maps (SOM), Learning Vector Quantization (LVQ), applications.
Module-4: [6 Hours]
Introduction to Fuzzy systems, Membership function, Fuzzy relational operation, Fuzzy IF THEN rules, Fuzzy Reasoning.
Module-5: [5 Hours]
Sugeno and Mamdani type systems, Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy systems, training methods, Application of ANN and Fuzzy systems to non-stationary time series prediction pattern classification.

Course Objective

1 .

To design and development of soft computing algorithms.
2 .

To analyze the real time problem and find solution to the same using soft computing techniques.

Course Outcome

1 .

1. To understand the fundamental concepts of Soft Computing techniques
2. To study and apply Artificial Neural Networks and different Learning techniques.
3. To understand and apply different Perceptron techniques.
4. To understand and analyse different techniques for data classification.
5. To study and analyse Fuzzy Set theory and its application.

Essential Reading

1 .

S. Haykin, Neural Networks - A Comprehensive Foundation, Peasrson Education, India

2 .

Jang, Sun and Mizutani, Neuro-Fuzzy and Soft-Computing – A computational approach to learning and machine intelligence, Prentice Hall of India

Supplementary Reading

1 .

S. Kumar, Neural Networks: A Classroom approach, Tata McGraw Hill

2 .

Martin T. Hagan, Howard B. Demuth, Mark H. Beale, Neural Network Design, Thomson

7493.t: ME6153: Intelligent Industrial Automation and its Application
7493.b:
Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : ME6153 : Intelligent Industrial Automation and its Application { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Module 1: Introduction to Industrial Automation and Intelligent Systems (3 Hours)
Introduction to Industrial Automation, Intelligent Systems,
Module 2: Use of Eclectic, Pneumatic and Hydraulic systems for Automation (9 Hours)
Use of pneumatic and electro pneumatic system for industrial automation, Use of electric drives and actuators, hydraulic and electro hydraulic system for industrial automation, Hydraulic Actuators for Industrial Automation, Pneumatic Actuators for Industrial Automation.
Module 3: Application of sensors for Automation (8 Hours)
magnetic sensors, ultrasonic sensors, infrared sensors, touch sensors, optical Sensors, gyro sensors, accelerometer, pressure sensors and Vision used for automation.
Module 4: Study of AI techniques for Automation (8 Hours)
Trajectory planning, Automation Algorithm, Use of fuzzy inference technique for industrial automation, Use of artificial neural network technique for industrial automation, Use of other AI techniques for industrial automation.
Module 5: Study and application controllers for Automation (8 Hours)
Study of various micro controllers and processors used for industrial automation, Study and application of hardware platforms required for industrial automation, Programming and flow control for automation.

Course Objective

1 .

1. To understand the fundamental concepts of automation.
2 .

2. To study and analyse electric, pneumatics and hydraulic systems for automation.
3 .

3. To explore different types of sensors for automation.
4 .

4. To analyse AI techniques for automation.
5. To gain knowledge on controllers and programming for automation.

Course Outcome

1 .

At the end of the course, students will be able:
1. To understand the fundamental concepts of automation
2. To explain electric, pneumatics and hydraulic systems for automation.
3. To use different types of sensors for automation.
4. To analyse and apply AI techniques for automation.
5. To use controllers and programming for automation.

7749.b:
Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : ME2362 : Thermal Engineering { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Module-1: Introduction: the concept of system, surroundings, equilibrium, Heat and work transfer, quasi-static process, temperature, and Zeroth law of thermodynamics. First Law of Thermodynamics: Internal energy, enthalpy, 1st law applied to non-flow and steady flow processes. (8 hours)
Module-2: Second Law of Thermodynamics: Clausius and Kelvin-Plank statements, Carnot cycle, corollaries, entropy, changes of entropy, or a perfect gas in various processes. (6 hours)
Module-3: Properties of Pure Substances: Definitions, p-V, p-T, T-s, and his diagrams for a pure substance, quality, Steam Tables, Charts for thermodynamics properties, Measurement of steam quality. (6 hours)
Module-4: Vapour Power Cycles: Rankine cycle, Comparison of Rankine and Carnot vapor cycles, Ideal working fluid for vapor power cycles. Air standard cycle: Otto, Diesel and Dual cycles, Fundamentals of SI, and CI engines. (7 hours)
Module-5: Conduction: Fourier law, Problem formulation, Boundary conditions, 1-D temperature solution, lumped system analysis. Convection: Forced and natural convection through flat plate and duct. Heat transfer coefficient correlations for laminar and turbulent convection. Radiation: Stefan-Boltzmann law, emissive power, emissivity and reflectivity, equivalent heat transfer coefficient for combined convection and radiation. (10 hours)

Course Objective

1 .

To present a comprehensive and rigorous treatment of classical thermodynamics from an engineering perspective.
2 .

To develop an intuitive understanding of thermodynamics by emphasizing the physics and physical arguments.
3 .

To present a wealth of real-world engineering examples to give students a feel for how basic thermal engineering is applied in engineering applications.

Course Outcome

1 .

Course Outcomes: At the end of the course, the student will be able to
CO1: Understand the basic concepts of thermodynamics like system, properties, equilibrium, temperature, and internal energy.
CO2: Quantify the second law of thermodynamics for a cycle and apply the principle of increase of entropy to evaluate the feasibility of a thermodynamic process.
CO3: Use the steam table for solving thermodynamic problems.
CO4: Distinguish between air standard and vapor power cycles.
CO5: Understand different modes of heat transfer and their applications to practical problems.

Essential Reading

1 .

V. Wylen and Sonntag, Fundamentals of Classical Thermodynamics, John Wiley , 2020

2 .

F. P. Incropera, D. P. DeWitt, T. L. Bergman, A. S. Levine, Introduction to Heat Transfer, Wiley , 2018

Supplementary Reading

1 .

P. K. Nag, Engineering Thermodynamics, Tata McGraw-Hill , 2017

2 .

J.P.Holman, Heat Transfer, Tata-McGraw Hill , 2017

6981.t: MM4106: Casting and Solidification of Metals
6981.b:
Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : MM4106 : Casting and Solidification of Metals { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Introduction: Casting as a process of Manufacturing. Moulding Processes, Equipments and Mechanization: Different types of Moulds, Moulding Materials and Moulding processes, Pattern and other mould making equipments, forces acting on moulds, Mould factors in metal flow, Moulding factors in casting design. Different types of binders and their uses in mould and core-makings.
Melting of Metals and Alloys for casting: Brief mention of various melting units, melting and post melting treatments, melting practices as adopted for a few metals and alloys such as CI, Al, Cu, steels, cast irons. Solidification of Metals and Alloys: Nucleation, Growth, Role of alloy constitution, Thermal
conditions and inherent nucleation and growth conditions in the liquid melt, Significance and practical control of cast
structure
Principles of Gating and Risering: Feeding characteristics of alloys, Types of Gates and Risers, Time of solidification and
Chowrinov rule, Wlodawer system for feeder head calculations, gating ratio, concept of directionality in solidification,
Yield of casting and prescription for its augmentation. Special casting Methods: Investment casting, Die casting,
Centrifugal casting, Full mould casting, Vacuum sealed casting. Casting Defects: A detailed analysis of casting defects.
Their causes and prescription of remedial measures.

Course Objective

1 .

Understanding of the overview of the different casting process
2 .

Understanding the design of mould
3 .

Learning of various defects arises during metal casting and their remedies
4 .

Analysis of Economics, Environment, Health and Safety Aspects, Various Application

Course Outcome

1 .

1. Students will be able to design pattern and mould.
2. Effect of different materials on mould and core designing.
3. They will be able to understand the different casting process and their on field applications.
4. Melting process used for different metals and alloys.
5. Students will be able to understand solidification and controlling process parameters to regulate the microstructure.
6. Understanding of different casting defects and the remedies.

Essential Reading

1 .

P. R. Beeley, Foundry Technology, Newnes-Buttterworths

2 .

P. D. Webster, Fundamentals of Foundry Technology, Portwillis press, Red hill

Supplementary Reading

1 .

P. C. Mukherjee, Fundamentals of Metal casting Technology, Oxford IBH

2 .

R. W. Hein, C. R. Loper and P. C. Rosenthal, Principles of Metal casting, Mc Graw Hill

Journal and Conferences

1 .

International Journal of Cast Metals Research

7237.b:
Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : SM6601 : Managerial Economics { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Fundamentals of Economics: Concept and Context, Difference between Micro and Macro Economics. Demand and Supply Analysis: Elasticity, Estimation and Forecasting. Production and Cost Analysis: Isoquant, Isocost, Revenue Analysis and Profit Maximization. Market Structure: Perfect Competition, Monopoly, Monopolistic, Oligopoly, Price and Output Determination, Short Run and Long Run Analysis. Oligopoly Market Structure and Models: Game Theory, Cournout’s Model, Kinked Demand Curve. Economics of Information: Adverse Selection Model Hierarchy, Principal Agent Model, Market Failure and Externalities. Macro-Economic Variables: Measurement of National Income, Inflation and Unemployment, Circular Flow of Income, Interrelationship. Product Market Equilibrium: Keynesian Theories of Income, Output Determination, Multipliers, Accelerator, Business Cycle. Principal Market Equilibrium: Determination of Interest Rates. Product and Financial Market: ISLM Model. Labour Market: Determination of Wages. Aggregate Demand, Aggregate Supply: All Market Equilibrium. Macro-Economic Policies: Monetary Policy, Fiscal Policy, Exchange Rate Policy. Macro-Economic Debate: Philip Curve, Sacrifice Ratio, Okun’s Law, Interaction of Output, Money Inflation, Interest Rates, Theories of Economic Growth and Models.

Course Objective

1 .

Understand fundamentals of microeconomics that apply at firm level
2 .

Understand fundamentals of macroeconomics that affect the economy

Course Outcome

1 .

The course will equip students to broaden the understanding on specific economic issues, problems and possible alternatives in diverse environments thereby promoting student interest in economics and the economy.

Essential Reading

1 .

Banerjee, S., Keat, K. G., and Young, P., Managerial Economics, Pearson Education , 6e

2 .

Shapiro, E., Macroeconomic Analysis., Galgotia Publication

Supplementary Reading

1 .

Blanchard, O., Macro Economics, Pearson Education. , 5e

2 .

Mankiw, N. G., Principles of Micro Economics., Thomson.
